evidence.passage: MPS shareholders reject CEO Lovaglio plan to fend off Intesa Sanpaolo takeover. (ANSA) - ROME, 29 OTT - The shareholders of Monte dei Paschi di Siena (MPS) on Thursday rejected two key parts of CEO Luigi Lovaglio's plan to fend off a 33-billion-euro takeover ‌bid by Intesa Sanpaolo for MPS, giving the thumbs down to offers for rival Italian lender Banco BPM and wealth manager Banca Generali. Over 91% of MPS's capital present at Thursday's meeting voted against the BPM move, with 6,47% in favour and 2.41%. The other part of Lovaglio's defensive plan, the bid for wealth manager Banca Generali, was rejected too. Votes against the proposal accounted for 90.9% of the capital present, while 6.66% voted in favour and 2.41% abstained. The rejection of both offers effectively puts a definitive end to the plan devised by Lovaglio to ward off Intesa Sanpaolo's attentions. Earlier on Thursday MPS's shareholders rejected a proposal for it to merge with Mediobanca, Italy's premier merchant bank, which it acquired earlier this year. The proposal needed the support of two-thirds of the bank's capital to be approved, but 63.65% voted against, with only 32.91% in favour and 3.42% abstaining. Intesa Sanpaolo had asked MPS's shareholders to reject the merger, in view of its takeover. (ANSA). Read article...

en.headline: Venice Council Approves Temporary Reuse of Private Buildings
en.subheadline: Resolution sets criteria and up to five-year terms, with public call for proposals pending.

body.text: The municipal council has approved a resolution that defines guidelines and criteria for the temporary reuse of privately owned buildings that are wholly or partially unused, according to the official document.
The allowed uses may last an initial maximum of three years and can be extended once for an additional two years, reaching a total possible term of five years.
The next step will be the publication of a public notice to collect and select proposals for such projects.

why_it_matters.text: The measure could help counter urban decay, foster regeneration and provide new services without consuming additional land.

what_next.text: A public notice will be issued to gather and evaluate proposals for temporary reuse.

key_facts.text: Maximum term for temporary reuse is three years, extendable once for two more years.
